conventions.convention: Gate labels denote exact SU(2) matrices. The compiler package is finite, inverse-closed and dense, with rational 0 < η₀ < 1/4096 and a supplied finite word net covering within η₀/4.

A target Cauchy name takes unary precision b and returns rational entry approximations with error at most 2⁻ᵇ; these approximants need not be unitary. Exact-real handles and Cauchy names are distinct interfaces.
The ideal recursion starts at level zero, uses ηⱼ₊₁ = 64ηⱼ^(3/2), and returns BCB*C*A. Exact comparisons and logarithms are ideal unit-cost operations.
With the supplied Pauli Y sign, (u·σ)(v·σ) = (u·v)I + i(u×v)·σ and [iu·σ,iv·σ] = −2i(u×v)·σ.

Bit complexity includes reading the complete positive binary numerator/denominator encoding of ε, which need not be reduced, and printing the expanded word. Gate coordinates have fixed algebraic descriptions.
Fixed-arity compilation assumes a supplied exact no-ancilla decomposition with m ≥ 1 one-qubit factors. Its scalar phase belongs to the entire unconditional block.

Controlled phase uses control-first lexicographic basis order. Replacing the three phase gates by Rz representatives multiplies CPθ by e^(−iθ/4); an additional control turns this scalar into a relative phase.

load_bearing.statement: For a fixed inverse-closed dense G ⊂ SU(2) and a certified base net of radius 0 < η₀ < 64⁻², the compiler returns, for 0 < ε ≤ η₀, a word W with ‖U−W‖ ≤ ε. Level-j length is at most L₀5ʲ; shared exact-real arithmetic uses O(3ʲ), separately from expanded output.

For the fixed algebraic gate package and base-net certificate, and a target Cauchy name of query time at most (b+1)^c, a deterministic implementation outputs W with ‖U−W‖ ≤ ε, length O(log^(log₍₃/₂₎5)(1/ε)), and bit time O((N+sε)^(c+10)), including input reading and expanded output.

For a supplied exact no-ancilla decomposition of U ∈ U(2^k) with m ≥ 1 one-qubit factors and c exact CNOTs, compiling the special-unitary factors to ε/m gives min|λ|=1 ‖U−λC‖ ≤ ε, gate count c+O(m log^(log₍₃/₂₎5)(m/ε)), and event-value change at most 2ε for every unit input and nonnegative contraction.
If D ∈ SU(2) and 0 ≤ ‖D−I‖ ≤ η ≤ 1/16, there are V,W ∈ SU(2) with ‖V−I‖, ‖W−I‖ ≤ √η and ‖D−VWV*W*‖ ≤ 40η^(3/2).
For the four stated SU(2) matrices, 0 ≤ η ≤ 1/16, factors within √η of I and approximants within η, the commutator difference is at most 4η^(3/2)+2η² ≤ 5η^(3/2).
The normalized lifts h=iH and t=e^(−iπ/8)T lie in SU(2) and generate a dense subgroup of SU(2); therefore the projective classes of H,T generate a dense subgroup of PU(2).

Under the stated fixed-dimension, polynomial-Cauchy input and conditioning hypotheses, the listed dyadic routines enclose their exact answers to diameter at most 2⁻ᵖ in O((p+B+1)^max(c,3)) bit operations; square roots include zero.

concerns.concern: Proof 5.1 says that the conditioning-bit bounds add along a derived-name chain and concludes query cost O(J(b+B+log L_J+1)^max(c,3)). The cited interval lemma's square-root construction instead requests approximately twice the output precision, which would multiply precision through nested layers. The additive bound needs an explicit conditioned square-root estimate for the positive balanced-branch radicand r/2. Since r > τ_j, the identity |√x−√y| = |x−y|/(√x+√y) supplies the required b+O(log(1/τ_j)) input precision. State this estimate and its use before summing guard bits; the stated complexity conclusion appears recoverable.

seams_checked.note: The fixed-arity theorem assumes a supplied exact factorization and explicitly leaves universal factorization existence to QC11; it imports no improved numeric CNOT bound.
The controlled-phase definition and global-phase-under-control identity match the control-first matrices and conjugate phase correction used here.
Exact Pauli matrices, Y orientation and H,T phases agree with the local products, normalized lifts and axis conjugations.

The finite-set QFT theorem uses the exact-real compiler with a rational tolerance inside its certified range, retains whole-circuit phases, and disclaims angle-generation bit time and outer-controlled compilation.

Normalized Clifford+T density is quoted correctly. Finite-dimensional synthesis invokes the finite-bit theorem on unconditional SU(2) factors and retains its fixed algebraic package and base-net requirements.
The output/cost definition cites the ideal compiler as a separate finite-gate approximation contract and makes no bit-time inference.
Determinant-one approximants use projective density as stated, then independently prove the finite-index and scalar-sign corrections.

The VMW suppliers establish their own algebraic dense package and fixed net, invoke the finite-bit compiler, and distinguish fixed hardcoded decomposition choices from variable-input equality tests.
